videos.script: Look at a real stylesheet and count how many times the same green appears. {{count}} On a small site, twenty. On a large one, two hundred. Now somebody decides the green should be a little darker. {{search}} Search and replace finds most of them. It also finds the one green that was meant to be different, and misses the one written in another format. {{var}} Custom properties fix this. You write the green once, give it a name, and use the name everywhere. Change it in one place and the whole site follows. {{inherit}} They do something a find-and-replace never could. They inherit, like a colour or a font. So a cancelled event can say: inside me, the accent is red. Everything inside it follows, with no new rules. {{dark}} That is also how dark mode is built. The same names, different values when the reader asks for dark. {{files}} The second half of the lesson is about the stylesheet as a whole. Which file holds what, in which order. How to name a component so nobody has to guess. {{layers}} And cascade layers, the newest tool here, which let you decide which group of rules wins before specificity is even asked. {{end}} Lesson 5 promised them. This is where they belong. {{close}}
